key_developments.event: Sancho III of Castile entrusts Calatrava castle to Raimundo of Fitero and Diego Velázquez.
Alexander III's Quanta et qualia confirms the order; affiliated with Cistercian observance.
Battle of Alarcos — order's army destroyed by Almohads; Calatrava lost.
Las Navas de Tolosa — order participates in decisive Reconquista victory.
Ferdinand the Catholic granted perpetual administration of the order's grand mastership.

_quarry.description: The first Iberian military order, founded in 1158 by Raimundo, abbot of the Cistercian abbey of Fitero, and the knight Diego Velázquez, to defend the recently-reconquered fortress of Calatrava on the Castilian frontier after the Templars judged the position indefensible. Confirmed by Alexander III's Quanta et qualia (1164) and brought under Cistercian observance. Calatrava played a central role in the 12th- and 13th-century Reconquista — notably at Las Navas de Tolosa (1212) — and its grand mastership eventually became a royal prerogative under the Catholic Monarchs in 1487.
